title: Check which shell your Mac user account starts with
summary: Find out which shell program is set as the default login shell for your macOS user account, for example /bin/zsh. These checks only read the setting and change nothing.

prerequisites: A Mac with a Terminal window open

steps.explain: Print your short user name, the name used in /Users/. Read-only.
steps.expect: One word with no spaces, for example alice. You need it in the next step.

alternatives.explain: Print the path of the default login shell saved for your account. Read-only. Look at the last part of the path: /bin/zsh means your Mac uses zsh. This is the account setting, so a window may run a different shell if it was changed there.
alternatives.expect: A path such as /bin/zsh, which is the default on current macOS. An older setup may print /bin/bash.

steps.explain: Read the UserShell setting of your account from the local directory database. Replace <USERNAME> with the name from the previous step. dscl only prints the record and changes nothing.

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: Your short macOS user name, from the previous step

steps.expect: A line such as 'UserShell: /bin/zsh'. Current macOS defaults to /bin/zsh; /bin/bash is also possible.
